verdict.rationale: Firecrawl's webhook docs list 'monitor check' as an event type that can notify an HTTPS endpoint when it starts, progresses, or finishes. That implies a first-party page-monitoring feature with push notifications, though the pack never describes how the monitor works. missing for 10: documentation of how monitors detect content changes (diffs, price or listing comparison), recurring check scheduling and frequency, notifications that fire specifically on detected changes rather than on check lifecycle, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can monitor target pages for content changes, such as price or listing updates, and get notified as they happen

citations.quote: Get notified the moment a crawl, batch scrape, extract, agent job, or monitor check starts, progresses, or finishes. Instead of polling for status, you provide an HTTPS endpoint
Verify that every webhook request actually came from Firecrawl by checking its HMAC-SHA256 signature.
